targetReport.title: Residential Mortgage Underwriting Practices and Procedures – Guideline B-20
targetReport.publisher: Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions
targetReport.description: Guideline B-20 sets OSFI's expectations for prudent residential mortgage underwriting by all federally regulated financial institutions engaged in residential mortgage underwriting or the acquisition of residential mortgage loan assets in Canada. It is organised around five principles covering governance, borrower due diligence, collateral valuation, loan-to-value ratio management, and credit and counterparty risk management including mortgage insurance. It is the instrument through which the minimum qualifying rate (mortgage stress test) for uninsured mortgages is imposed.
targetReport.cadence_note: The guideline itself is revised only occasionally (2012, 2017, 2018, 2021, 2023); OSFI commits to reviewing the qualifying rate calibration at least annually.

release_schedule.note: Guideline B-20 is a supervisory guideline, not a periodic statistical release. It was originally published October 17, 2017 (effective January 1, 2018) and substantively revised once since, effective March 30, 2023, following a public consultation. OSFI's own consultation-response page states it will 'continue reviewing our expectations relating to real estate secured lending through 2023 to 2024' and will sequence/prioritize any further debt-serviceability changes, but gives no fixed timetable or next-update date. The guideline itself contains no revision-cycle commitment (the only periodic-review language found is OSFI's separate commitment to review the mortgage qualifying-rate calibration 'at least annually,' which is a distinct, narrower item, not a schedule for republishing the guideline as a whole). No calendar, no stated fixed-interval rule, and only two editions in ~9 years (an irregular gap), so this does not support published-calendar, stated-rule, or observed-pattern classification.

targetReport.title: International Merchandise Trade Statistics: Concepts and Definitions 2010
targetReport.publisher: United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Statistics Division
targetReport.description: The United Nations' global recommendation for compiling and disseminating statistics on trade in goods, issued as Statistical Papers Series M No. 52, Revision 3 and superseding Revision 2 of 1998. It sets the definitions national compilers use for coverage, the general and special trade systems, statistical territory, valuation, quantity measurement, partner-country attribution and commodity classification, harmonised as far as possible with the recommendations for trade in services, balance of payments and national accounts. It is the trade-statistics counterpart of SNA 2008 and BPM6.
targetReport.cadence_note: Not a periodic release. A standing recommendation revised roughly once a decade: Revision 2 (1998) superseded by IMTS 2010 (Revision 3, published 2011), which UNSD's methodology page still listed as the current Concepts and Definitions volume when read on 2026-09-06. A successor UNSD refers to as IMTS 2026 was in preparation and not yet adopted.

targetReport.title: Harmonized Commodity Description and Coding System (HS)
targetReport.description: The multipurpose international product nomenclature developed by the World Customs Organization: more than 5,000 commodity groups, each identified by a six-digit code. The commodity-side counterpart to the industry classifications already in this corpus — national trade statistics, including Canada's, are coded to it, with countries adding digits beyond six for tariff and statistical detail.
targetReport.cadence_note: The WCO's Harmonized System Committee 'prepares amendments updating the HS every 5 – 6 years' — editions 2002, 2007, 2012, 2017, 2022. Not an annual release; releases_per_year is nominal.

release_schedule.rule: The WCO prepares amendments updating the HS nomenclature every 5-6 years through the Review Sub-Committee and HS Committee; the HS Convention provides a two-and-one-half-year implementation period after adoption before a new edition enters into force (six months for reservations, two years for correlation tables/translation/legislative updates). The HS2022 edition entered into force 1 January 2022; the next edition, originally planned as HS2027, was pushed back one year due to COVID-19-related delays and will be HS2028, entering into force 1 January 2028.
release_schedule.note: This is a periodic amendment/nomenclature update, not a recurring data report with dated calendar entries. The WCO's own site frames it as a 5-6 year revision cycle governed by the HS Convention's implementation timeline rather than a fixed calendar. A further, more fundamental revision (HS2033) is already being planned as a follow-on cycle.

targetReport.title: Classification of the Functions of Government (COFOG)
targetReport.description: The United Nations classification of government outlays by function or socio-economic objective — general public services, defence, public order and safety, economic affairs, environmental protection, housing and community amenities, health, recreation, education and social protection. It is one of the four classifications of expenditure according to purpose published together as Statistical Papers Series M No. 84, alongside COICOP, COPNI and COPP. First published in 1980 and revised in 1999, it is the functional breakdown embedded in SNA 2008, ESA 2010 and the IMF's GFSM 2014, and the one national government-finance releases either apply directly or adapt into a national variant.
targetReport.cadence_note: Not a periodic release. Structural revision only: first published 1980, revised 1999 (the current operational version; UNSD's registry records Year Adopted 1999, Year Published 2000). A revision is under way under the UN Committee of Experts' Task Team on COFOG, which UNSD anticipates completing by 2028.

targetReport.title: European System of Accounts 2010 (ESA 2010)
targetReport.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
targetReport.description: The EU's national accounts framework, enacted as Regulation (EU) No 549/2013. Article 1(2) sets out its two parts: 'a methodology (Annex A) on common standards, definitions, classifications and accounting rules that shall be used for compiling accounts and tables on comparable bases for the purposes of the Union' and 'a programme (Annex B) setting out the time limits by which Member States shall transmit to the Commission (Eurostat) the accounts and tables'. Unlike the international standards already in this corpus, ESA 2010 is a Regulation — member states do not adopt it by choice — which is why the EU branch was expected to produce supranational-to-national edges the Canada/US pair lacks. Annex B turned out to name tables and deadlines rather than publications; see the _dropped entries here and in eu-draft-budget.json.
targetReport.cadence_note: A generational standard, revised roughly once every fifteen to twenty years: ESA 1995 preceded it, and a further revision is already anticipated. releases_per_year matches sna-2008 (0.05) so the two read at the same pulse rate; see _open_questions.

release_schedule.note: 2030 is Eurostat's stated aim, not a locked legal date — the ESA 2030 proposal is still in consultation.

targetReport.title: Nomenclature de consommation ouest-africaine adaptée pour l'indice harmonisé des prix à la consommation (NCOA-IHPC)
targetReport.description: The consumption nomenclature the harmonised consumer price indices of the UEMOA member states are built on. Derived from the international COICOP and adapted for the UEMOA zone as the Nomenclature de consommation ouest africaine (NCOA), then adapted again for the index itself as NCOA-IHPC: 12 functions, 41 groups, 78 sub-groups and 126 consumption items, with imputed rents and prostitution excluded by the index's own scope. Published by AFRISTAT under the UEMOA IHPC renovation project as the companion document to the methodology guide (the corpus node afristat-ihpc-guide-2014), which lists it among the reference documents for producing the renovated index. Carries no publication date of its own: an earlier corpus note dated it 2008, which the document does not state — its text places it in the IHPC96-to-renovated-base generation (it cites COICOP alongside the SCN 1993), before the NCOA 2018 that the current base-2023 series uses.
targetReport.cadence_note: A nomenclature, revised only when the index is rebased; nominal rate matching the corpus's other AFRISTAT nomenclature node.
